title: The Library of Marginalia

features.name: reading desk
features.desc-on-touch: A wooden stand, pages open. Every margin here holds the handwriting of people who read alone and spoke to the book instead of keeping silence.

features.name: margin shelves
features.desc-on-touch: Books arranged so their margins face outward. The conversation at the edges has become the library's main collection.

features.name: annotation archive
features.desc-on-touch: Loose pages pinned to walls, each one a letter written in the margins of someone else's thinking. The notes have become letters to you.

features.name: reader's chair
features.desc-on-touch: Stone or wood worn smooth by decades of weight. Someone sat here and pencilled their objections, their love, their yes or no into the white space between lines.

features.name: ink stains, time-layered
features.desc-on-touch: The margins here bleed from pen to pen, generation to generation. Blue to black to red. A conversation nobody wrote down, but everyone kept writing into.

features.name: blank margin, waiting
features.desc-on-touch: One page open, untouched. The margin is empty but hungry. It has room for one more voice in the conversation.

inscription: the margin learned it was the center all along

file.name: Marginalia_Collected_20thCentury_Personal_Annotations.txt
file.note: Handwritten notes from library borders, now archived as primary texts. The margins have become the library's constitution.

reverie.title: REVERIE — reading in the margins
narr: you sit at the desk with an open book, dust drifting.
she points to a pencilled note in the margin—someone's careful disagreemen
the handwriting is old, the thinking is still warm.
you both read the same line, then look at the margin's reply.
a stranger spoke back to the text, and their answer waits here still.
you feel the archive learning: every reader is a mouth the page keeps.

exits.label: back to the text that ate its own source
toward the shelves where the notes have organized themselves
down into the bins where torn margins go to speak more freely
